code: policy_softmax <- function(temperature = 0.1) {   stopifnot(     is.numeric(temperature),     length(temperature) == 1,     is.finite(temperature),     temperature > 0   )   structure(     list(temperature = temperature),     class = c("softmax_policy", "bandit_policy")   ) }

title: Creating custom bandit policies
text: policy_state() receives arm names environment must return policy state fields added. can called repeatedly, always build state scratch .
code: policy_state.softmax_policy <- function(policy, arms, ...) {   policy$arms <- arms   policy$pulls <- setNames(rep(0L, length(arms)), arms)   policy$reward_sum <- setNames(rep(0, length(arms)), arms)   policy }

title: Creating custom bandit policies
text: select_arm() must return list arm. Returning propensity, marginal probability selected arm, optional strongly recommended: makes resulting logs usable importance-weighted offline evaluation. Softmax makes easy selection probabilities explicit. Two details worth copying: subtracting maximum exponentiating keeps calculation numerically stable, randomness comes current RNG (never call set.seed() inside method, break engine’s reproducibility guarantees).
code: select_arm.softmax_policy <- function(policy, t, ...) {   estimates <- ifelse(     policy$pulls > 0,     policy$reward_sum / pmax(policy$pulls, 1),     0   )   centred <- (estimates - max(estimates)) / policy$temperature   probabilities <- exp(centred) / sum(exp(centred))   index <- sample.int(length(policy$arms), 1, prob = probabilities)   list(     arm = policy$arms[[index]],     propensity = probabilities[[index]],     reason = "softmax"   ) }

title: Creating custom bandit policies
code: update_state.softmax_policy <- function(policy, arm, reward, t, ...) {   policy$pulls[[arm]] <- policy$pulls[[arm]] + 1L   policy$reward_sum[[arm]] <- policy$reward_sum[[arm]] + reward   policy }

title: Bandits for RAN optimisation: 5G NR link adaptation
text: transmission opportunity scheduler picks MCS. higher MCS carries bits per resource element likely fail decoding (NACK). useful quantity delivered spectral efficiency: MCS spectral efficiency block decoded, zero otherwise. arms eight entries NR PDSCH MCS table 64QAM (3GPP TS 38.214, Table 5.1.3.1-1). Values spectral efficiency bit/s/Hz.

title: Bandits for RAN optimisation: 5G NR link adaptation
text: Per-opportunity SINR Gaussian dB around user’s mean SINR, standard deviation 3 dB (stand-fast fading interference fluctuation). MCS decoding threshold attenuated Shannon bound, SINRm=10log⁡10(2SEm/η−1)\text{SINR}_m = 10\log_{10}\!\left(2^{\,\text{SE}_m/\eta} - 1\right) η=0.75\eta = 0.75. probability ACK logistic curve gap realised SINR threshold, slope 1.5 per dB. reward delivered spectral efficiency normalised [0, 1]: r=𝟙{ACK}SEm/SEmaxr = \mathbb{1}\{\text{ACK}\}\,\text{SE}_m / \text{SE}_{\max}. expected reward arm computed numerical integration, banditlab can report exact pseudo-regret. Three users represent cell edge, middle cell cell centre. different best MCS:
code: eta <- 0.75 slope <- 1.5 sigma_db <- 3 threshold_db <- 10 * log10(2^(se / eta) - 1)  p_ack <- function(sinr_db, mcs) {   1 / (1 + exp(-slope * (sinr_db - threshold_db[[mcs]]))) }  expected_reward <- function(mean_sinr_db) {   vapply(names(se), function(m) {     ack <- integrate(       function(s) p_ack(s, m) * dnorm(s, mean_sinr_db, sigma_db),       mean_sinr_db - 8 * sigma_db, mean_sinr_db + 8 * sigma_db     )$value     ack * se[[m]] / se_max   }, numeric(1)) }  draw_reward <- function(mcs, mean_sinr_db) {   sinr <- rnorm(1, mean_sinr_db, sigma_db)   ack <- runif(1) < p_ack(sinr, mcs)   as.numeric(ack) * se[[mcs]] / se_max }  round(threshold_db, 1) #>  MCS0  MCS4  MCS8 MCS12 MCS16 MCS20 MCS24 MCS27  #>  -6.2  -1.3   2.9   5.8   9.9  14.3  19.3  22.3 scenarios <- c(cell_edge = 5, mid_cell = 12, cell_centre = 18) mu_table <- sapply(scenarios, expected_reward) round(mu_table, 3) #>       cell_edge mid_cell cell_centre #> MCS0      0.042    0.042       0.042 #> MCS4      0.105    0.108       0.108 #> MCS8      0.156    0.211       0.212 #> MCS12     0.123    0.297       0.305 #> MCS16     0.030    0.344       0.460 #> MCS20     0.001    0.153       0.567 #> MCS24     0.000    0.011       0.300 #> MCS27     0.000    0.001       0.093 apply(mu_table, 2, function(x) names(which.max(x))) #>   cell_edge    mid_cell cell_centre  #>      "MCS8"     "MCS16"     "MCS20"

code: policy_static_rule <- function(reported_sinr_db) {   structure(list(reported_sinr_db = reported_sinr_db),             class = c("static_rule_policy", "bandit_policy")) } pick_mcs <- function(sinr_db) {   ok <- names(threshold_db)[threshold_db <= sinr_db]   if (length(ok) == 0) names(threshold_db)[1] else ok[length(ok)] } policy_state.static_rule_policy <- function(policy, arms, ...) {   policy$arms <- arms   policy$choice <- pick_mcs(policy$reported_sinr_db)   policy } select_arm.static_rule_policy <- function(policy, t, ...) {   list(arm = policy$choice, propensity = 1, reason = "cqi_table") } update_state.static_rule_policy <- function(policy, arm, reward, t, ...) {   policy }

title: Bandits for RAN optimisation: 5G NR link adaptation
text: OLLA standard industry mechanism. adds offset reported SINR: step_down dB NACK, step_down * target / (1 - target) dB ACK, drives block error rate (BLER) target (10% ). positive reward means block decoded, policy can read ACK/NACK reward.
code: policy_olla <- function(reported_sinr_db, target_bler = 0.1, step_down = 0.5) {   structure(     list(reported_sinr_db = reported_sinr_db, target_bler = target_bler,          step_down = step_down,          step_up = step_down * target_bler / (1 - target_bler)),     class = c("olla_policy", "bandit_policy")   ) } policy_state.olla_policy <- function(policy, arms, ...) {   policy$arms <- arms   policy$offset <- 0   policy } select_arm.olla_policy <- function(policy, t, ...) {   list(arm = pick_mcs(policy$reported_sinr_db + policy$offset),        propensity = 1, reason = "olla") } update_state.olla_policy <- function(policy, arm, reward, t, ...) {   policy$offset <- policy$offset +     if (reward > 0) policy$step_up else -policy$step_down   policy }

title: Bandits for RAN optimisation: 5G NR link adaptation
text: policy_thompson() Beta-Bernoulli rejects rewards 0 1. Delivered spectral efficiency continuous, use standard binarisation trick (Agrawal Goyal, 2012): reward r∈[0,1]r \[0, 1], update posterior Bernoulli(rr) draw. expected update unchanged, policy targets arm.
code: policy_thompson_binarised <- function(alpha = 1, beta = 1) {   structure(list(prior_alpha = alpha, prior_beta = beta),             class = c("thompson_binarised_policy", "bandit_policy")) } policy_state.thompson_binarised_policy <- function(policy, arms, ...) {   policy$arms <- arms   policy$alpha <- setNames(rep(policy$prior_alpha, length(arms)), arms)   policy$beta <- setNames(rep(policy$prior_beta, length(arms)), arms)   policy } select_arm.thompson_binarised_policy <- function(policy, t, ...) {   draws <- rbeta(length(policy$arms), policy$alpha, policy$beta)   list(arm = policy$arms[[which.max(draws)]], propensity = NA_real_,        reason = "posterior_draw") } update_state.thompson_binarised_policy <- function(policy, arm, reward, t, ...) {   b <- as.numeric(runif(1) < reward)   policy$alpha[[arm]] <- policy$alpha[[arm]] + b   policy$beta[[arm]] <- policy$beta[[arm]] + 1 - b   policy }

what: A policy that forgets: discounted Thompson sampling
title: Bandits for RAN optimisation: 5G NR link adaptation
text: Stationary Thompson sampling accumulates evidence forever, change keeps trusting MCS20 long time. Discounted Thompson sampling (Raj Kalyani, 2017) decays every arm’s counts factor gamma step, keeping effective memory around 1 / (1 - gamma) observations. OLLA uses CQI reported start (18 dB + 3 dB bias) must track change offset alone; real scheduler also receive new CQI reports, baseline pessimistic OLLA.  Mean dynamic regret per replicate, phase
code: policy_discounted_thompson <- function(gamma = 0.99, alpha = 1, beta = 1) {   structure(list(gamma = gamma, prior_alpha = alpha, prior_beta = beta),             class = c("discounted_thompson_policy", "bandit_policy")) } policy_state.discounted_thompson_policy <- function(policy, arms, ...) {   policy$arms <- arms   policy$s <- setNames(rep(0, length(arms)), arms)   policy$f <- setNames(rep(0, length(arms)), arms)   policy } select_arm.discounted_thompson_policy <- function(policy, t, ...) {   draws <- rbeta(length(policy$arms), policy$s + policy$prior_alpha,                  policy$f + policy$prior_beta)   list(arm = policy$arms[[which.max(draws)]], propensity = NA_real_,        reason = "discounted_posterior_draw") } update_state.discounted_thompson_policy <- function(policy, arm, reward, t, ...) {   b <- as.numeric(runif(1) < reward)   policy$s <- policy$gamma * policy$s   policy$f <- policy$gamma * policy$f   policy$s[[arm]] <- policy$s[[arm]] + b   policy$f[[arm]] <- policy$f[[arm]] + 1 - b   policy } change_at <- 1001 reps2 <- 100 env_drift <- bandit_drifting_sinr(18, 8, change_at, horizon)  res2 <- run_experiment(   env_drift,   policies = list(     olla        = policy_olla(18 + cqi_bias_db),     ucb1        = policy_ucb1(),     thompson    = policy_thompson_binarised(),     dts_0.99    = policy_discounted_thompson(gamma = 0.99),     dts_0.998   = policy_discounted_thompson(gamma = 0.998)   ),   horizon = horizon,   replications = reps2,   seed = 2026,   keep_trajectories = TRUE ) mu_before <- expected_reward(18) mu_after <- expected_reward(8) tr <- as.data.frame(res2$trajectories) after <- tr$step >= change_at tr$mu_arm <- ifelse(after, mu_after[tr$arm], mu_before[tr$arm]) tr$mu_best <- ifelse(after, max(mu_after), max(mu_before)) tr$inst_regret <- tr$mu_best - tr$mu_arm tr <- tr[order(tr$policy, tr$replicate, tr$step), ] tr$cum_regret <- ave(tr$inst_regret, tr$policy, tr$replicate, FUN = cumsum)  band <- aggregate(cum_regret ~ policy + step, data = tr[tr$step %% 20 == 0, ],                   FUN = function(x) c(mean = mean(x),                                       lo = unname(quantile(x, 0.1)),                                       hi = unname(quantile(x, 0.9)))) band <- do.call(data.frame, band) names(band)[3:5] <- c("mean", "lo", "hi")  ggplot(band, aes(step, mean, colour = policy, fill = policy, linetype = policy)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_vline(xintercept = change_at, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +   scale_colour_banditlab() + scale_fill_banditlab() +   theme_banditlab() +   labs(title = "Dynamic cumulative pseudo-regret",        subtitle = "Mean SINR drops from 18 dB to 8 dB at step 1,001; band = 10th-90th percentile",        x = "Transmission opportunity", y = "Cumulative pseudo-regret",        colour = "Policy", fill = "Policy", linetype = "Policy") final <- tr[tr$step == horizon, ] phase <- aggregate(inst_regret ~ policy + I(step >= change_at),                    data = tr, FUN = sum) names(phase) <- c("policy", "after_change", "regret") phase$regret <- phase$regret / reps2 wide <- reshape(phase, idvar = "policy", timevar = "after_change",                 direction = "wide") names(wide) <- c("policy", "regret_before_change", "regret_after_change") best_after <- names(which.max(mu_after)) share_after <- aggregate(I(arm == best_after) ~ policy,                          data = tr[tr$step > horizon - 200, ], FUN = mean) names(share_after)[2] <- "best_mcs_share_last_200" knitr::kable(merge(wide, share_after), digits = 2,              caption = "Mean dynamic regret per replicate, by phase")

title: Regret definitions used by banditlab — regret_definitions
text: package uses exact definitions. Let \(\mu_a\) true expected reward arm \(\), \(\mu^* = \max_a \mu_a\), \(A_t\) arm selected step \(t\). Instantaneous pseudo-regret step t: \(\Delta_{A_t} = \mu^* - \mu_{A_t}\). Recorded per decision trajectories. Cumulative pseudo-regret T steps: \(R_T = \sum_{t=1}^{T} (\mu^* - \mu_{A_t})\). Recorded checkpoints , final step, summary. Expected regret: Monte Carlo mean final cumulative pseudo-regret across replicates, reported summary.bandit_result(). Optimal action share: fraction steps selected arm attains \(\mu^*\). Realised regret (comparing observed rewards counterfactual draws optimal arm) computed version. quantities require known expected rewards. Environments declare (bandit_custom() without expected_rewards) yield NA every regret metric; baseline invented.
